observations: Photo 0 shows a car gearbox/transmission assembly on the ground with wiring/hoses attached; no clear make/model markings visible.
Photo 0 shows the bellhousing area and internal clutch/torque-converter-looking components; condition appears used with dirt/debris.
Photo 1 shows the same transmission/gearbox from another angle; multiple hydraulic lines/wiring harnesses are visible.
No visible label/part number/vehicle VIN plate in either photo to confirm Rogue vs Altima or exact gearbox type.

claims.claim: Direct tokunbo Japan highest grade Rogue and Altima gearbox
claims.evidence: Photos show a transmission assembly but no readable brand/part number/label or any Japan/vehicle-specific identification.

risks.risk: Exact vehicle fitment is unclear (Rogue vs Altima, and which engine/gearbox variant). Wrong variant can be incompatible with mounts, sensors, and ECU/TCU programming.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the gearbox identification plate/label or stamped part number (and any transmission code) plus a photo of the mating side showing connector/sensor layout.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used gearbox with unknown compatibility (worst case: may not fit or may require parts/programming).

risks.risk: Working condition is unknown (could be damaged internally, have leaks, or missing components).
risks.proof: Video/clip of the gearbox being tested (bench test or installed test) showing it engages all gears and no abnormal noise; or a receipt/diagnostic report from a test run.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: treated like it may be faulty and may need overhaul).

risks.risk: Missing parts/accessories (solenoids, sensors, harness connectors, cooler lines, mounting brackets) not visible in these angles.
risks.proof: Photo checklist: all external sensors/solenoids, connectors, mounting brackets, and any included harnesses laid out clearly; close-ups of connector ends.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown completeness (worst case: buyer may need to source missing sensors/lines/brackets).

risks.risk: Transmission type (CVT vs automatic, etc.) is not confirmed from photos; wrong type affects pricing and compatibility.
risks.proof: Photo of the transmission type label or internal identifier; or a clear shot of the CVT/AT-specific components and part number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lowest-case category for an unknown transmission type (worst case: not the expected type).

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of any gearbox ID plate/label and the stamped part number/transmission code.
Send photos of all external sensors/solenoids/connectors and confirm nothing is missing (include mounting brackets and any harnesses).
Provide a short video of the gearbox being tested/engaging gears (or installed test) and show no leaks.
Confirm which exact Rogue/Altima model year and engine (and whether it’s CVT or automatic) the gearbox came from.
response.reason: The photos show a used transmission assembly, but there’s no readable identification to confirm the exact Rogue/Altima variant or transmission type, and working condition is not provable remotely. Proof is needed to price confidently.
